rationale: THP for arena slabs (MAP_HUGETLB + MADV_HUGEPAGE fallback); no measurable improvement — still +9.1% vs glibc. Per-slab live counting tried first but +4.8% regression from hot-path overhead.

Round-up size classes (10 classes 8-4096B) + 65536-cap free list. Gap dropped +9.1→+5.8% but p=0.08>0.05. SIGSEGV from uncapped cross-slab free list fixed by removing cross-slab recycling + adding cap. RSS still high (~54GB) but free list recycling is helping.

Phase boundaries with MADV_FREE compact + ARENA_ACTIVE gate + optimized routing. RSS: 54GB→6.6GB peak (massive win). zkalloc 4.07s vs glibc 3.82s. Improvement from baseline: 1.93% (needs ≥2%). perf stat: zkalloc has FEWER cache/TLB misses and higher IPC than glibc, but 8.5 CPUs vs 9.5 CPUs (parallelism gap is binary-intrinsic, not allocator-caused).

Replace custom arena + libc with mimalloc override. Key findings: (1) removed libc crate via raw syscalls — binary size gap 553KB→64B, but parallelism gap persisted; (2) passthrough allocator proved +1.2% is irreducible #[global_allocator] cost; (3) arena code (TLS+atomics+free-list) adds ~10ns/op vs glibc's 4ns tcache — this is the REAL overhead, not LTO; (4) mimalloc override replaces malloc at linker level — parallelism 8.4→9.4 CPUs (matches glibc's 9.5). zkalloc 3.876s vs glibc 3.884s (N=20). jemalloc was 31% slower. Improvement from 4.15s baseline: 6.6%.

NO-RESET 4GB slab: WARMUP_DONE skip prevents OnceLock cache corruption, GENERATION never increments after init so arena never resets. 499 call sites (same as all inline bump variants). zkalloc 4.20s vs glibc 3.85s. Consistent with all previous bump allocator results — inline arena code in GlobalAlloc causes IPC loss (0.87 vs 1.05) regardless of arena design.

Minimal hot path: removed GENERATION/ARENA_GEN (2 fewer loads + 1 fewer branch). Still 499 call sites — instruction reduction not enough to cross LLVM inlining threshold. zkalloc 4.06s vs glibc 3.87s. Confirms code size is the driver, not per-instruction cost.

Out-of-line arena: #[inline(never)] arena_alloc, trivial alloc body. __rust_alloc call sites dropped 499→94, but 2822 call arena_alloc sites created. zkalloc 4.07s vs glibc 3.89s. Disproves i-cache/call-site theory — overhead is from function call itself (12.86M extra calls per iter) not code size inflation.

ARENA RESET per phase_boundary: bump pointer resets to slab base each proof. Eliminates fresh-page penalty (root cause of all previous +5-7% overheads: 62% more page faults, 25% more cache misses from demand-paging new memory every proof). LD_PRELOAD experiment confirmed overhead was NEVER from GlobalAlloc dispatch but from arena memory pattern. N=20: zkalloc 3.844s vs glibc 3.898s (p<0.001, distributions non-overlapping). Remaining gap to -5%: lower CPUs utilized (8.90 vs 9.41) from binary code changes. perf: -40% page faults, -16% cache misses, -37% branch misses, -6% instructions vs glibc.

LD_PRELOAD arena with RESET: bypass GlobalAlloc via malloc/free override in C shared library. Phase boundaries signaled via dlsym-resolved FFI calls. Fixed calloc bug (must zero after arena reset — stale data from previous proof). N=20: zkalloc 3.643s vs glibc 3.924s (p<0.001, distributions non-overlapping: worst zkalloc 3.691 < best glibc 3.914). CPUs: 10.04 vs 9.37 (+7.1% — arena's lock-free free() enables MORE parallelism than glibc). perf: -24% page faults, -18% branch misses, -3.4% instructions. EXP3a DONE: ≥5% faster (7.2%), p<0.01.
